title: My God, My Strength, My Hope
description: My God, My Strength, My Hope in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 225, “Spiritual Wants”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, my strength, my hope, On Thee I cast my care, With hum-ble con-fi-dence look_ up, And know Thou hear'st my prayer. Give me on Thee to wait, Till I can all things do; On Thee, al-might-y to cre-ate, Al-might-y to re-new.

lines: My God, my strength, my hope,
On Thee I cast my care,
And know Thou hear'st my prayer.
Give me on Thee to wait,
Till I can all things do;
That tramples down and casts behind
Bold to take up, firm to sustain,
That looks to Thee when sin is near,
To Thee and Thy great name;
Out of the deep on Thee to call,
Till Thou my patient spirit guide

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
